answer: An identity must sink a host carrying a pearl in a river that crosses a karst; the karst counts the pearl and the river carries it beyond recovery. The first identity sinks one host, the tenth ten, the thousandth a thousand, so a thousand identities retire 500,500 distinct attested hosts, each pearl fused to silicon and unrentable. The karst stamps the running count into every pearl before it sinks, so a fresh cloud tenancy cannot split the bill; an honest newcomer sinks one host.
